text:
> "initiation... is the removal of impurity and with that fundamental impurity is removed karma and maya... beyond Maya... pure reality levels... tiny latent impression... all that separates you from finally attaining Shiva."
> "When you're in Shambhavuppaya, you're experiencing pure nirvikalpa. Not a trace of thought consciousness."
> "As long as it does not become permanent, the Shambhava state degenerates back into the Shambhava means,"
> "We find joy in practicing awareness of being of consciousness. Why? Because that consciousness is the source of all things. The bliss we feel from that is the bliss of emanation."
> "Anashrita Shiva means Shiva who has not come out from himself into the world of creation... he has entered into himself... he does not have the support of anything else, he is self-sustaining."
> "That which is to be taught. Because it is the cause of what is rightly known... He is the cause of all that is glorious and laudable."
[karma_and_rebirth.md ~01:08:40-01:22:00 (txt 295-320)]
[Anava/karma/mayi mala; Maya as Sankhya-like substance; tattvas to Maya then pure; Kashmiri nondual: impurity = objectivity/difference, lack of free consciousness.]
[kundalini_pt2.md 00:49:21,139 --> 00:49:29,079]
[All Shiva/Shakti union described here takes place in Shambhava state behind the veil of thought; without nirvikalpa there could be no vikalpa (point credited to Tantraloka's opening).]
[sources_tantraloka.md 00:26:01,039 --> 00:26:11,220]
[Cardinal difference from Kaula/Krama sources where Shambhava is ultimate; here still in domain of practice while subtle duality remains.]
